one_line: Branches AI conversations into a visible, revisitable thinking graph.
what_it_does: A visual workspace for branching questions, connected sources, investigations, and design directions.
leverage_rationale: Structured branching state and connected evidence are genuinely useful, but a general agent could reproduce much of the workflow with UI driving, albeit with friction.
leverage_evidence: Pitch centers on visible paths that can be branched and revisited.
About text describes investigate and design modes with sources kept connected.
execution_rationale: The packet presents a coherent multi-view product and the frame sheet shows a substantial visual workspace plus an associated AI conversation, though no end-to-end tool invocation is visible.
execution_evidence: Frame sheet shows connected-node workspace, alternate views, and AI-chat workflow.
About text describes multiple workspace modes and source-connected investigations.
impact_rationale: Knowledge workers, researchers, and creative thinkers have a clear need to preserve branching exploration rather than lose it in linear chat.
impact_evidence: Pitch identifies the limitation of linear AI conversations.
About text describes research and creative-work use cases.
creativity_rationale: The visible trail/branching interaction is a fresh synthesis of chat and graph-based thinking, pursued across research and design.
creativity_evidence: Frame sheet visibly combines branching maps with conversational AI.
Product framing treats the exploration path as the durable artifact.
usability_note: The map-and-chat model appears understandable, though density may challenge larger investigations.
red_flags: No explicit WebMCP tool-call evidence in the submitted frame sheet.
standouts: Strong visual metaphor and coherent branching workspace.
advance_reason: Clear concept, meaningful audience value, and credible product evidence despite limited direct tool-call proof.

one_line: Uses typed WebMCP tools to make difficult web workflows accessible to agents and users.
what_it_does: An appointment-booking portal whose drag-only calendar can be operated through high-level typed tools with live narration.
leverage_rationale: The deliberately hostile scheduling widget is exactly where structured in-page tools change reliability and accessibility, replacing brittle coordinate interaction.
leverage_evidence: About text specifies a drag-and-drop-only calendar with no click fallback.
Seven typed tools cover provider search, availability, booking, and notes; actions are narrated through aria-live.
execution_rationale: The scope is tightly defined and the stated workflow is coherent, but the packet lacks readable direct visual proof of the complete booking flow.
execution_evidence: About text gives a concrete natural-language booking scenario and tool-based implementation.
Demo is reported alive and frame sheets were submitted.
impact_rationale: Screen-reader users and people blocked by complex custom widgets are a specific audience with a serious, well-established accessibility problem; the product directly addresses it.
impact_evidence: About text identifies interactive-widget failures as a leading screen-reader barrier.
Live narration and high-level tools preserve human awareness and control.
creativity_rationale: Reframing WebMCP as an accessibility bridge, with a deliberately difficult calendar as the test case, is an original and ambitious interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Agent executes complex scheduling without dragging or clicking the widget.
Human-in-control narration is integrated into the concept.
usability_note: Natural-language booking and narrated actions should substantially reduce interaction burden; accessibility coverage beyond the demo is unclear.
red_flags: Visual details and end-to-end booking completion are not verifiable from the accessible packet text alone.
standouts: Strong accessibility rationale and high WebMCP indispensability.
advance_reason: Exceptional fit between the problem and structured WebMCP interaction, with strong audience value.

one_line: An agent-native weighted random draw application.
what_it_does: Lets users manage entries, weights, exclusions, and single or multi-winner draws through shared app state and WebMCP tools.
leverage_rationale: Structured tools make repeated draws and state updates reliable, but general UI automation can achieve the same simple outcome without much friction.
leverage_evidence: About text lists tools for adding, updating, drawing, and resetting exclusions.
Demo sequence is a small set of ordinary random-draw operations.
execution_rationale: The described scope is coherent and likely functional, but no video frame sheet was submitted and the central workflow is not visually demonstrated.
execution_evidence: About text specifies a concrete eight-planet demo sequence.
Demo is reported alive; no frame sheets submitted.
impact_rationale: Random draws serve identifiable audiences such as educators, facilitators, and game hosts, but the packet establishes limited differentiated value beyond convenience.
impact_evidence: Product supports weighted and multi-winner draws.
About text frames agent operation as the primary use case.
creativity_rationale: Agent-native framing and shared state add a new angle to a familiar utility, but the underlying concept is simple.
creativity_evidence: Application is designed around discoverable structured capabilities.
Demo includes weights, exclusions, renaming, and multi-winner draw.
usability_note: The operation set is simple and likely easy to understand.
red_flags: No submitted video frames; product claims are primarily textual.
advance_reason: Coherent but low-delta utility with thin evidence and limited ambition.

one_line: Connects CAD, simulation, manufacturability, and supplier evidence into a traceable review workspace.
what_it_does: Helps engineers and agents inspect active design context, compare manufacturing evidence and quotes, and prepare bounded next steps with human approval.
leverage_rationale: Revision-aware structured evidence and bounded approvals address state and traceability problems that generic UI agents handle poorly.
leverage_evidence: About text emphasizes active revision, current evidence, assumptions, and approval authority.
Workspace combines Onshape, CNC checks, SimScale workflow, and supplier comparison.
execution_rationale: The product has a coherent professional workflow and careful handling of unknown costs, but the packet does not prove all integrations end-to-end.
execution_evidence: About text describes preview rather than automatic CAD edits.
Quotation workspace separates unit price, setup, shipping, tax, and unknown values.
impact_rationale: Manufacturing engineers have a concrete high-cost problem: translating changing CAD and scattered evidence into safe production decisions.
impact_evidence: Pitch targets CAD-to-manufacturing review.
Traceability links findings and quotations to designs and assumptions.
creativity_rationale: The synthesis of CAD context, simulation evidence, supplier quotes, and human-gated agent actions is ambitious and notably focused.
creativity_evidence: Human approval is built into proposed geometry corrections.
Supplier-document preservation and comparison are part of the same evidence model.
usability_note: Evidence-oriented review should improve confidence, though the breadth of integrations may add complexity.
red_flags: No direct readable frame analysis available for verifying integrations.
standouts: Strong traceability and safety framing for agent-assisted engineering.
advance_reason: High-value domain workflow with substantial WebMCP delta and credible, safety-conscious scope.

one_line: A real-time hide-and-seek game where an agent rewrites its hunter code mid-match.
what_it_does: The human hides in a ray-traced light world while an agent receives sparse sensors and improves a bounded seeker bot through WebMCP.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP is the game mechanic: it gives the agent structured sensing and code-rewrite actions while preserving the intended blind-player constraint.
leverage_evidence: About text says the agent wins by rewriting the built-in bot during the match.
Agent receives small sensor readings and a full rulebook through WebMCP rather than UI control.
execution_rationale: The rules, timing, sensing, energy/noise/scent mechanics, safe code limits, and visible rewrite state form a coherent complete game pitch; visual end-to-end proof is still limited.
execution_evidence: About text specifies a three-minute objective and real-time mechanics.
Canvas engine and bounded safe API are described; frame sheets were submitted.
impact_rationale: It offers credible entertainment and a memorable demonstration of agent intelligence as adaptation rather than speed.
impact_evidence: Clear playable survival objective.
Agent intelligence is made legible through mid-match code improvement.
creativity_rationale: Real-time hide-and-seek against an agent that rewrites its own hunter is a genuinely memorable interaction model with ambitious constraints.
creativity_evidence: Sparse once-per-second sensing and code evolution create a distinctive challenge.
Dark 2D light world and hidden-depth premise reinforce the concept.
usability_note: Simple survival goal and visible game state support playability; agent difficulty may vary by model.
red_flags: Model-dependent difficulty and hidden-depth behavior may be inconsistent.
standouts: WebMCP is integrated into the core competitive loop rather than bolted on.
advance_reason: Highly original game mechanic and unusually strong WebMCP integration.

one_line: A privacy-preserving shopper-to-merchant demand loop with human-gated offers.
what_it_does: Connects a private closet and merchant studio so agents identify needs, propose margin-safe offers, and generate claim-safe promotions without exposing identity.
leverage_rationale: Page-local tools, shared state, locked facts, atomic validation, and human-only approvals create a reliable privacy and compliance workflow that generic UI driving cannot comparably reproduce.
leverage_evidence: About text describes 21 tools across closet and studio, with human-only Approve, Lock facts, and Bought actions.
Promo claims are rejected atomically against locked facts and export is blocked while claims are wrong.
execution_rationale: The packet articulates a coherent end-to-end loop with explicit privacy, margin, and claim-safety constraints, though the broad system is not directly demonstrated in video evidence.
execution_evidence: Concrete under-a-minute closet-to-offer flow is described.
Unknown shipping remains unknown rather than defaulting to zero.
impact_rationale: Shoppers benefit from useful recommendations without identity surveillance, while merchants get demand signals and compliant promotions.
impact_evidence: Product shares only category, size, and need/want rather than identity or wardrobe rows.
Merchant offers are constrained by locked margin rules.
creativity_rationale: The privacy-preserving two-sided loop and deliberate absence of agent powers are unusually thoughtful and original for commerce tooling.
creativity_evidence: Human-only release and purchase actions are central design choices.
Hem-loop metaphor matches the hidden structural role of the product.
usability_note: The one-approval flow is attractive, but two-sided setup and policy constraints may be complex.
red_flags: Claims about live cross-surface behavior are not fully visually verifiable in the packet.
standouts: Excellent privacy, consent, and claim-safety boundaries.
advance_reason: Distinctive, safety-conscious commerce workflow with transformative structured-agent leverage.

one_line: A radiology viewer that lets an agent arrange and analyze workflow state without reading scans.
what_it_does: Adds a WebMCP layer to OHIF for study comparison, windowing, slice navigation, measurement propagation, undo, and measurement-grounded report drafting.
leverage_rationale: WebGL viewer state is difficult to scrape or manipulate reliably; typed tools expose safe, precise actions while explicitly preventing pixel access and diagnosis.
leverage_evidence: Transcript shows tool calls moving both studies to requested slices and applying human approval.
About text states no tool returns pixels and measurement proposals use IDs rather than coordinates.
execution_rationale: The transcript provides unusually strong end-to-end evidence: natural-language request, live tool calls, synchronized viewer changes, human-in-loop approval, undo, measurements, and grounded report drafting.
execution_evidence: Video transcript explicitly describes real-time tool invocation and synchronized slice changes.
Transcript covers approval toggle, undoability, measurements, and report drafting.
impact_rationale: Radiologists face a real, high-friction workflow problem, and the product reduces navigation burden while keeping clinical judgment and pixel interpretation human-controlled.
impact_evidence: About text identifies prior-study arrangement and state management as workflow burdens.
Every report sentence is tied to accepted measurements and export integrity is enforced.
creativity_rationale: The safety boundary—agent can operate everything except read the scan—creates a novel and deeply pursued human-agent collaboration model.
creativity_evidence: Agent propagates measurements and drafts findings without receiving pixels.
Signature binds report text to measurements and invalidates altered exports.
usability_note: Natural-language arrangement and reversible actions should materially improve radiology workflow, subject to specialist validation.
red_flags: Mock data is used; clinical deployment claims should not be inferred.
standouts: Best packet-level evidence and exceptionally clear safety model.
advance_reason: Strongest combination of transformative WebMCP leverage, verified workflow, impact, and originality.

one_line: A browser-resident agent workspace that builds and exports websites with frontend, backend, and shop capabilities.
what_it_does: Uses WebMCP tools to write pages, compile Rust blocks in-browser, manage products, roll back generations, and export a static site.
leverage_rationale: Site-specific typed tools, generation rollback, compilation, and shared live preview are materially more reliable than generic browser driving, though the category is familiar.
leverage_evidence: About text describes typed tools for file writing, compilation, product management, rollback, and export.
All work runs in a service worker with live preview next to chat.
execution_rationale: The packet describes an ambitious coherent browser-only workflow and frame sheets were submitted, but no direct end-to-end video proof is available.
execution_evidence: Frontend, backend, shop, undo, and export are presented as one workflow.
About text specifies browser compilation and static-host export.
impact_rationale: Indie builders and small businesses have a credible need for lower-friction site creation without external toolchains or providers.
impact_evidence: Pitch targets complete website creation from a browser page.
Shop and export features extend beyond a toy mockup.
creativity_rationale: Compiling a Rust backend block inside the browser and combining it with an agent-built storefront is ambitious and memorable.
creativity_evidence: No server and no external providers are claimed; service-worker execution is central.
Numbered generations and rollback make agent editing reversible.
usability_note: Conversational creation and rollback are approachable, but login and complex build concepts add onboarding burden.
red_flags: Claims are broad and technical; full backend and commerce flow are not directly proven here.
standouts: Ambitious browser-only compilation and rollback model.
advance_reason: High ambition and meaningful agent-native development workflow, with some evidence limitations.

one_line: Turns particle-physics questions into shared, replayable 3D investigations.
what_it_does: Lets learners query linked particle data, configure a live Three.js scene, compare particles, reveal force networks, and save editable evidence notebooks.
leverage_rationale: Structured scene configuration and durable, replayable findings substantially improve on asking an agent for a text answer or driving a dense 3D UI manually.
leverage_evidence: About text lists eleven tools for data queries, scene configuration, comparisons, networks, and notebook saving.
Saved findings capture the exact scene and can be reopened, revised, undone, and shared.
execution_rationale: The concept and feature set are coherent, but there is no direct video transcript and no gallery imagery; end-to-end visual completion is not verifiable.
execution_evidence: About text describes shared visible state and one-URL sharing.
Demo is reported alive, but no frame sheets were visually confirmable.
impact_rationale: Learners and educators have a real need for inspectable visual explanations of relationships that are hard to understand from tables or prose.
impact_evidence: Product targets Standard Model symmetries and force relationships.
Editable notebooks preserve evidence and learner control.
creativity_rationale: The combination of natural-language inquiry, live 3D scientific scene construction, and replayable evidence is a fresh educational interaction.
creativity_evidence: Exact scene state is saved with each finding.
Agent and learner share and revise the same visible Three.js investigation.
usability_note: Replayable visual investigations should aid learning, though 3D scientific interfaces can be cognitively demanding.
red_flags: No accessible gallery images or transcript evidence in the packet.
standouts: Strong durable-artifact approach to agent-assisted science learning.
advance_reason: Good educational fit and original replayable visualization concept, tempered by thin visual evidence.

one_line: Captures grounded browser sources and turns them into a continuing learning loop.
what_it_does: Pins exact passages with context and reasons, then supports short study paths, checks, plans, recommendations, and learner-approved notebook handoffs.
leverage_rationale: Persistent source-grounded state across browsing, study surfaces, and recommendations is valuable, though much of the capture and learning workflow could be approximated by a general agent with friction.
leverage_evidence: About text says exact passage, source page, surrounding context, and reason are preserved.
The same Pin moves across browser side panel, app, Gemini, Notebook, Board, Learn, Plan, Check, and Insights.
execution_rationale: The packet describes a complete learning loop and extensive surfaces, but frame-level technical tool evidence is unavailable.
execution_evidence: About text covers capture, learning, correction, recommendations, and handoff.
Seven gallery images and three frame sheets are reported.
impact_rationale: Students and lifelong learners have a clear problem: useful ideas encountered while browsing are disconnected from later understanding and action.
impact_evidence: Product grounds study in the original source rather than detached summaries.
Short one-, three-, and five-minute paths target realistic learner constraints.
creativity_rationale: The source-pinning-to-learning-manager loop is a fresh synthesis with a notably broad but coherent cross-surface ambition.
creativity_evidence: Learner-approved Google Notebook handoff preserves source grounding.
Corrections and completed outcomes influence future recommendations.
usability_note: Short paths and preserved context make the workflow approachable; cross-product handoffs may add complexity.
red_flags: Broad architecture claims exceed what can be verified without readable frame analysis.
standouts: Strong evidence-led learning loop anchored to exact browser sources.
advance_reason: Clear audience need and thoughtful source-grounded workflow, with moderate WebMCP differentiation.
